India has emerged as a standout emerging market following the US midterm election results, with the Nifty gaining 6.8 per cent and the rupee appreciating 1.1 per cent to close at ₹93.81 against the US dollar on November 6. India’s 10-year government bond yield also declined by 12.5 basis points, according to a report by Shriram Research.

The land acquisitions trend across reflects a shift towards a more cautious, strategic and opportunity-driven approach to real estate development.

It shows developers are increasingly prioritising the quality of land parcels over the scale of acquisition. Factors such as location, connectivity, development potential, land pricing and expected demand are becoming central to investment decisions. The growing adoption of Joint Development Agreements (JDAs) highlights the industry’s preference for capital-efficient development models. Rather than committing substantial capital towards outright land purchases, developers are exploring partnerships that allow them to manage financial exposure while pursuing viable projects.

This changing investment approach also creates an opportunity for Tier-2 cities to emerge as alternative growth destinations for real estate developers. These markets offer opportunities to acquire strategically located land parcels, develop projects at relatively competitive entry costs and cater to an expanding base of homebuyers and businesses.

Going forward, we expect land acquisition strategies to become more decentralised, with developers increasingly evaluating emerging cities alongside established metropolitan markets. The focus, however, will remain on locations backed by genuine economic activity, infrastructure visibility and sustainable end-user demand.

The initiative aims to build advocacy for integrating financial literacy into formal school education, recognising it as an essential life skill.

It seeks to bring together policymakers, educators, parents, government bodies, education boards and industry experts to drive this agenda.

The initiative will feature Investor Awareness Programmes (IAPs) across educational institutions to engage students and encourage grassroots participation.

The National Centre for Financial Education (NCFE) and Central Depository Services (India) Limited (CDSL) have joined the initiative as Knowledge Partners.

A dedicated Mission Wealthwise landing page will serve as a content hub for the initiative.

TACC Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of HEG Advanced Materials Limited (HEGAM) and part of the LNJ Bhilwara Group, has received the approval letter for an incentive of Rs 609.50 crore under the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India. The incentive is for TACC’s Synthetic Graphite Anode Material project at Sirsoda Industrial Area, Dewas, Madhya Pradesh, and is subject to scheme guidelines and prescribed conditions.

Spread across more than 100 acres, the Dewas facility is planned for a committed scalled capacity of beyond 30,000 metric tonnes per annum (MTPA) by FY2028-29. The first phase of 20,000 MTPA is targeted for commissioning by June 2027.

In a significant milestone for Bihar’s urban development and municipal finance landscape, the maiden municipal bond issuance by Patna Municipal Corporation (PMC) was listed on the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) in the presence of Hon’ble Chief Minister of Bihar, Shri Samrat Choudhary in a ceremonial event held on 10th November in Patna.

The issuance marks the first-ever municipal bond by an Urban Local Body (ULB) in Bihar and represents an important step towards mainstreaming capital market financing for urban infrastructure development in the State and the Country.

With a base issue size of ₹100.03 crore and a green-shoe option of ₹99.96 crore, the private placement received subscription of over 2 times the base issue size from institutional investors, reflecting strong investor confidence and growing appetite for municipal instruments. The proceeds from the bonds will be utilised to finance 15 projects to be undertaken by the PMC for Rs 199.99 crore for the redevelopment of the market areas of Patna for improving urban services, public convenience and economic efficiency.

Sagar Defence Engineering Limited (SDE), an Indian deep-tech company specialising in unmanned and autonomous defence systems, has raised ₹300 crore (approximately USD 33 million) from Indian institutional investors at a pre-money valuation of ₹20,000 crore (approximately USD 2.2 billion) as part of its pre-IPO fundraising.

The investment marks a significant milestone in the company’s decade-long journey, from a modest 150 sq. ft. workspace to a technology-driven defence enterprise. It also reflects growing institutional confidence in India’s ability to develop indigenous, globally competitive deep-tech solutions in strategically important sectors.
